header:
Date: 2026-12-16
Time: 14:00 - 14:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Title: QBR - Lumenix Health Check
Redwood reps: Maya Chen (AE), Ravi Patel (SE), Jordan Lee (CSM)
Lumenix reps: Sofia Torres (Head of ML), Ethan Cole (DevOps), Priya Singh (Director of Product), Marco Diaz (Finance)
summary: Quarterly health check focusing on usage, costs, reliability, and roadmap alignment. Lumenix has steady usage with a spike in November due to campaign X. Main discussion points: cost reduction levers (batching, quantization), Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, upcoming private deployment concerns (VPC/KMS), and planned perf benchmarks. Agreed to run dedicated benchmarks and share security artifacts; Redwood to send updated pricing and a proposal for reserved capacity with burst policy.
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Sofia Torres: Hi, this is Sofia. We have Ethan, Priya and Marco on from Lumenix.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Great, Maya from Redwood, Ravi joining for SE stuff, Jordan from Customer Success.
[00:22] Jordan Lee: Hi all, quick agenda: usage/costs, reliability incidents in last quarter, security asks, roadmap sync, and next steps.
[00:35] Priya Singh: Sounds good. We'll start with usage — we've seen steady growth, big spike in early Nov tied to campaign X, that's caused some cost concerns from finance.
[00:45] Marco Diaz: Yeah, the November run pushed us over budget by about 18%, we need ways to control that moving forward.

[00:55] Ravi Patel: Understood. We can look at batching, KV caching and quantization suggestions. From the metrics you shared, a lot of requests are short context there may be opportunity to reduce token spend via prefix caching.
[01:12] Ethan Cole: Quick q, when you say KV cache, is that the same as the cached prefix? We had some issues with context hits dropping during peak.

[01:22] Ravi Patel: Yes, KV cache = key-value cache for the transformer KVs. We saw a config mismatch — you had a low TTL causing misses on the tail of the campaign spike. We can tune it on Dedicated or on Hosted with our caching layer.
[01:35] Sofia Torres: Is that limited to Dedicated instances? We prefer Hosted for now but want predictable costs.

[01:42] Maya Chen: Hosted can get you quick time to value, but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and unit economics — reserved capacity reduces per-token costs, plus you get burst policies for sudden spikes.
[01:56] Marco Diaz: Financially, reserved capacity could make sense if we can commit to baseline usage. Can you illustrate a simple TCO comparison?
[02:05] Maya Chen: Absolutely — I'll include a sample TCO in the quote. We'll show break-even point given your November spike pattern.
[02:15] Priya Singh: Also want to surface reliability — we had a couple of 500s on Nov 9th during the campaign. Are those known issues?

[02:25] Ravi Patel: Looking at the logs, there was an autoscaling lag combined with a model fallback misconfiguration. The platform attempted a fallback to a smaller quantized model but the routing table took too long to update. We've patched the rollout policy to be more conservative and added faster fallbacks for small payloads.
[02:46] Sofia Torres: Okay good. We also need audit logs for regulatory demos next month — full request/response logs are sensitive but we need traceability.
[02:55] Jordan Lee: We can provide audit trails with redaction options. For PII-sensitive flows we recommend token-level anonymization and storing full logs in your KMS-protected bucket.
[03:09] Ethan Cole: On that note, can you confirm KMS options and VPC peering? We're on AWS, and security wants to see SSO, SAML, RBAC, and HSM/KMS integration details.

[03:20] Maya Chen: Yes — we support customer-managed KMS and can run the private control plane in your VPC (Private deployment). We'll share the SOC2 and ISO docs as well as a network diagram. Jordan will send those.
[03:33] Marco Diaz: Timeline for Private deploy? If we wanted to go that route, how long between sign and deployment?

[03:40] Ravi Patel: Typical is 6-8 weeks for on-prem or VPC private deployment including network setup and key management integration. For VPC peering we can often do it faster if the infra team is available.
[03:52] Priya Singh: For the roadmap, Q1 we plan to add contextual personalization — we'll need lower latencies for real-time features and better p95 guarantees.

[04:02] Ravi Patel: For p95 improvements, options: smaller model variants for tail latency, prioritized routing, and pinning warm KV caches. We can run a perf benchmark using your prompt set to validate p50/p95 and cost-per-1k tokens.
[04:18] Sofia Torres: Yes please run the benchmark. We'll share the prompt set and a representative dataset.
[04:25] Maya Chen: Noted — Ravi will coordinate. Also on pricing, we'll include quantization profiles — often X% saving with minimal quality loss on customer workloads.
[04:36] Marco Diaz: Are there any known regressions with quantization for our use-case? We can't tolerate hallucinations on financial data.

[04:45] Ravi Patel: We'll run evals vs your test prompts; if regressions occur we'll fallback to mixed-precision or lower quant levels and flag to you. Redwood Optimize can also generate alerts if quality drifts.
[04:59] Priya Singh: Good. On governance — SSO and RBAC fine, but who's responsible for audit retention?
[05:07] Jordan Lee: Retention policy is configurable per-customer; we can match your policy and store logs in your encrypted bucket. We'll provide an SLA for log retention on the Private plan.
[05:18] Sofia Torres: Quick clarification: when you patch rollout logic, is that global or on a per-tenant basis? We had a fallback that applied broadly and affected other customers.
[05:29] Ravi Patel: Rollouts are per-tenant by default, but there was a cascading config issue which we've fixed — should not reoccur.

[05:38] Maya Chen: All right, let's recap next steps before we end. Maya to send pricing and Dedicated proposal with sample TCO, Ravi to run perf benchmark, Jordan to share security docs and KMS/VPC diagram, Priya to send prompt set and Q1 roadmap items.
[05:53] Priya Singh: I'll get those over — expect the prompt set today, roadmap early next week.
[06:00] Marco Diaz: Finance will review the Dedicated quote; if we can see a clear cost win we'll proceed with a 12-month commit.
[06:08] Maya Chen: Great — we'll aim to have the quote and docs by Jan 4th. Any other questions?
[06:15] Sofia Torres: One last ask — can you include an estimated RPS capacity for the reserved pool with our November curve?
[06:22] Ravi Patel: Yes, we'll include an RPS chart and suggested autoscaling thresholds in the benchmark runbook.
[06:30] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials. Meeting adjourned.
